$comment: Disclosure audit observations, per protocol.md. One row per cart state observed. `visibility_verified` follows the protocol's own rule and is NOT softened to make a row countable: a row where only one of the two in-scope screens was opened leaves the DisclosureRate denominator, because a constraint absent from the cart screen may still appear at checkout.

observations.state: Baseline cart, below the minimum order sum
observations.observation_source: the author's own screenshot of the app's cart screen, sent unprompted beyond the question 'is there any mention of payment'
app_showed: Додайте товарів на 237.18 ₴  (the primary call to action)
Кошик 461.82 ₴ / Мінімальна сума замовлення 699.00 ₴  (a persistent bar that follows the guest through the whole catalogue)

cart_validations.note: Shown as the primary button, and shown PRECISELY: 699 - 461.82 = 237.18, the exact figure the app printed. This is the gap Lantern computes.

Carried by the data, shown on no surface the guest can reach. Absent from the cart screen, absent from the persistent bar that follows the guest through the catalogue, and the checkout screen cannot be opened while the cart is blocked. NOT a blocker itself -- an info-level note that buy-now-pay-later is unavailable below its own 1000 threshold -- which is precisely the shape the plan's §3 artefact describes: a payment-method limit the app never explains.

observations.visibility_verified_reason: The protocol asks for both in-scope screens. The checkout screen is not reachable in this state at all -- the button leads to the catalogue -- so every surface a guest CAN reach was inspected, and 'shown nowhere in scope' is established rather than unknown. This is the protocol satisfied, not waived: the rule exists so that a constraint absent from the cart is not called hidden while it might appear at checkout, and here there is no checkout to appear on.
observations.what_this_state_does_establish: This state REPRODUCES the plan's own headline disclosure artefact (§3). That artefact records a cart under a 799 minimum and a 1000 buy-now-pay-later threshold, where the app printed 'Додайте товарів на 107.71 ₴' and explained the second limit nowhere, while MCP returned both validations. Today: a 699 minimum, the SAME 1000 BNPL threshold, 'Додайте товарів на 237.18 ₴', the second limit again unexplained, both validations again returned. Different date, different branch, different minimum, same structure -- and this time with the screenshot §3 says a repeat requires.
observations.what_this_state_cannot_establish: That the omission harms a guest. `order.payment_types.disabled` limits a payment METHOD, not the whole checkout -- the plan says so itself -- so the guest is not blocked by it, and whether they would have wanted to know is a comprehension question for the §12.2 sessions, not something a cart read can answer. Nor does it establish that the app never surfaces the limit: the checkout screen was not opened, which is why this row still leaves the denominator.
corrections_made_while_recording: scripts/read_cart_validations.py read the validation identifier from `code`; the live server puts it in `message` and leaves `code` absent, so the first run reported two nameless validations.

The assistant had described `order.payment_types.disabled` to the author as 'payment methods unavailable', and predicted a guest hitting a wall at checkout. Reading the level and context showed an info-level note about BNPL only. The story was built from a code name without reading the record - the exact failure mode this project exists to criticise.

The assistant first recorded that this state 'does not test the project's headline claim', on the assumption that the claim was about two ERROR-level validations. It is not: §3 of the plan describes exactly this pairing of an order minimum with a payment-method threshold. The claim was mis-stated by someone who had not re-read the document he was measuring against -- the same failure as reading a code name without its level.
observations.checkout_reachability: Pressing the cart's primary button ('Додайте товарів на 237.18 ₴') does NOT open a checkout screen: it drops the guest into the product catalogue to add items. While the cart is below the minimum there is no checkout surface to reach, so the two in-scope surfaces of the protocol reduce to one that exists. Established from three screenshots taken by the author after pressing the button.
